comparator.name: Bachelor in Philosophy of a Specific Discipline
comparator.route: Economics and Business Economics discipline route
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations for RIO programme 57084, published on the current ESPhil programme-regulations page. The TER defines a 180-EC curriculum consisting of 90 EC in one chosen academic discipline, 60 EC of eight named common philosophy courses, 15 EC of discipline-specific philosophy electives, and a 15-EC bachelor-thesis and milestones trajectory linking both fields. The normalized target is generic and does not name a discipline. The Economics and Business Economics route is instantiated under the neutral route rule: the TER lists Erasmus School of Economics first among the eligible EUR schools, and its broad Economics and Business Economics bachelor is selected rather than a narrower specialist programme. This choice was fixed independently of UCR fit. The 90-EC discipline component and the 15-EC discipline-specific philosophy component are preserved at their official structural weights. The public curriculum describes the economics programme's foundations, while the exact 2026 discipline-elective pair is available only through MyEUR; no unpublished course choice or EC subdivision is invented.

routeSelection.route: Economics and Business Economics discipline route
routeSelection.basis: The generic target permits several chosen disciplines. No discipline represents the programme more strongly than the others. The TER lists Erasmus School of Economics first among the eligible EUR schools, and Economics and Business Economics is the broad, general economics-and-business bachelor rather than a specialist ESE programme. It is therefore selected by the neutral least-specialized and official-order rules, before and independently of UCR course selection.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, economics & business
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR's philosophy core with economics, business, finance, public policy, governance and quantitative research. The label names both sides of the programme and does not imply that UCR offers the external degree's full 90-EC philosophy sequence.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible response to the selected Economics and Business Economics route: philosophical study of knowledge, mind, ethics and political authority is combined with a substantial economics, business, finance, governance and research-methods sequence.
progression: Introduction to Western Philosophy, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the two programme strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes every economics course that formally requires it, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. The 100-level rhetoric course precedes Persuasive Communication. Ethics and Philosophy of Mind precede the 300-level philosophy courses conceptually. The final semester brings together econometrics, behavioural economics, finance and qualitative methodology. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, society & law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines philosophy with a sustained law sequence and with sociology, international relations, conflict, history and rhetoric. The label therefore states the programme's legal and social-institutional content rather than presenting it as a philosophy or law degree alone.
alternatives.concept: A programme organised around the philosophical examination of law, social institutions and global power: the philosophy core is combined with public, private, criminal, constitutional and EU law, plus sociology, international relations, conflict studies, history and argument.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the economics, business, finance, accounting and quantitative-economics sequence and replaces it with Law, Society & Justice; public international, criminal, constitutional, private and EU law; sociology and advanced social theory; international relations and conflict; and historical research. Thirteen of the 24 courses differ. The organising choice is therefore legal and social-institutional analysis rather than the philosophical examination of economics and business.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later law course with that formal prerequisite. Introduction to Sociology precedes advanced contemporary social theory. Introduction to Western Philosophy, Ethics and Philosophy of Mind establish the philosophical foundation before the 300-level philosophy courses. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Persuasive Communication. Introductory law and society courses come before the advanced private-law, EU-law, conflict and research work in the final year. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, health & human existence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum joins philosophy of mind, emotion, agency, ethics and rights to substantial biomedical, public-health and health-psychology study. The label captures that combination without implying that UCR offers a medical degree or a full philosophy-of-medicine sequence.
alternatives.concept: A programme organised around philosophical questions of human existence, mind, health, illness and responsibility: ethics and metaphysics are combined with biomedical science, public health, psychology and evidence-based health research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces the economics, business, finance, governance, rhetoric and econometrics sequence with foundations in life science and brain and behaviour, followed by cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory work, anatomy, pathology, pharmacology, infection and immunity, epidemiology, health psychology and research synthesis. Sixteen of the 24 courses differ. Compared with the society-and-law route, it likewise differs by sixteen courses. The educational choice is sustained scientific and psychological study of health and human life rather than institutional or economic analysis.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior begin the programme and precede every dependent life-science, biomedical and psychology course. Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology, Biochemistry and Functional Anatomy precede the advanced pathology, pharmacology, infection and disease-mechanism courses. Introduction to Western Philosophy precedes Ethics and Philosophy of Mind, which in turn precede Philosophy of Emotion and Free Will, Time & the Self. Medical & Health Psychology precedes the final research seminar and lifespan course. Personal & Professional Development remains within Year 1. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic programme interests, the common philosophy core, the Liberal Arts and Sciences combination, and the two economics/business directions represented by the neutrally selected comparator route. Two further coherent generator-backed directions remain. Social and behavioural sciences, law, international social challenges, global power and sociology form one institutional route, included as Philosophy, Society & Law. Medicine and healthcare form a second route, included as Philosophy, Health & Human Existence. Both are mechanically feasible and qualitatively distinct; the pairwise differences are 13 courses between the first two alternatives and 16 courses for each pair involving the health alternative. The history, culture and communication direction is separately recorded but is not pursued after the maximum of three included alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both introduce major Western philosophical traditions and the historical development of philosophical questions; the Erasmus component concentrates on the Enlightenment while UCR provides the broader introduction.
Both examine what it means to be human through mind, consciousness and personal identity.
Both are the central moral-philosophy component, joining ethical theory to contemporary applied questions.
Both examine technology philosophically. UCR concentrates on artificial intelligence, human flourishing, fairness and responsibility rather than art and media more broadly.

Theoretical Analytic Philosophy is a dedicated survey of analytic philosophy. UCR distributes related work across philosophy of mind, metaphysics and political philosophy and has no single equivalent course.
The comparator includes a dedicated Philosophy of Science course. UCR teaches research methods and evidence evaluation but no philosophy-of-science course, so the component is left unmatched.
The comparator provides a systematic historical epistemology course. UCR's introductory philosophy course is already aligned with Enlightenment, and no separate UCR epistemology course exists.

The comparator requires a 15-EC independent thesis integrating philosophy and the chosen discipline. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so it is recorded as unmatched; UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

The comparator's chosen-discipline component comprises 90 EC of Economics and Business Economics coursework. It is preserved as the official 90-EC component rather than equated with one UCR course; the UCR economics and business courses appear separately in this block.

The comparator reserves 15 EC for philosophy courses tailored to economics. UCR combines philosophy and economics across separate courses but has no verified equivalent 15-EC discipline-philosophy package.
Both are political-philosophy components examining authority, society and critique through major arguments and thinkers.

notes.text: The Rotterdam programme combines 90 EC from a separate chosen discipline with a structured 60-EC philosophy core, 15 EC of philosophy tailored to that discipline, and a 15-EC integrative thesis. UCR instead combines individual philosophy courses directly with courses from economics and business, law and society, or health and biomedicine. UCR offers philosophy in ethics, mind, emotion, agency, political thought, human rights and AI, but it does not reproduce Rotterdam's dedicated sequence in analytic philosophy, epistemology and philosophy of science or its discipline-specific philosophy package.
